questions.prompt: What happens to a Node.js HTTP server if a route runs a synchronous 500ms CPU loop (e.g., `pbkdf2Sync` or huge regex)?

options.text: Other requests run in parallel on V8
The single event loop freezes for 500ms, stalling every other connected client and health check

questions.prompt: Why must graceful shutdown handle `SIGTERM` by closing the HTTP server AND closing DB/Redis pools with a timeout?

options.text: Orchestrators (Kubernetes/ECS) send `SIGTERM` before `SIGKILL`; draining in-flight requests and closing pools prevents dropped responses and leaked DB connections

questions.prompt: What is the risk of `process.on('uncaughtException', () => {})` (swallowing the error and keeping the server running)?

options.text: Nothing; it makes the server 100% reliable
The process may be left in a corrupted half-initialized state with leaked sockets; log the error, shut down, and let the supervisor restart

questions.prompt: Match each Node.js production bottleneck to its root cause.

rows.label: Steadily climbing RSS / heap until OOM kill

columns.label: Synchronous CPU work or `JSON.parse` on huge payloads on main thread
Unbounded in-memory caches, unclosed streams, or growing listener arrays
Unclosed file handles or unpooled outbound sockets

questions.prompt: Why should `http.Server` timeouts (`requestTimeout`, `headersTimeout`, `keepAliveTimeout`) be tuned behind a load balancer like ALB or Nginx?

options.text: If Node's `keepAliveTimeout` is shorter than the load balancer's idle timeout, the LB can send a request on a closing socket and return a spurious `502`

questions.prompt: Select all practices that prevent Prototype Pollution and injection vulnerabilities in Node.js APIs. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Validate and strip unknown fields from `req.body` at the API boundary (e.g., Zod)
Use parameterized SQL queries and `execFile` with `shell: false`
Recursively `target[k] = src[k]` on raw `JSON.parse` input without key checks
Reject or strip `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype` keys when merging untrusted objects (or use `Map` / schema validation)

questions.prompt: What is ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service) in Node.js?

options.text: Evil/nested quantifier regexes taking exponential time on crafted input and freezing the single-threaded event loop

questions.prompt: Why is `structured logging` (e.g., `pino` writing JSON to `stdout`) faster and better than `console.log` in high-RPS Node services?

options.text: `console.log` is synchronous on TTY/some streams and unstructured, whereas `pino` formats JSON with minimal overhead and request correlation IDs

questions.prompt: What happens when an Express/Node route forgets `return` before `res.status(400).json(...)`?

options.text: Execution continues past `res.json(...)`, often calling `res.json(...)` a second time and throwing `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`

questions.prompt: How should you scale a stateless Node.js HTTP service across an 8-vCPU machine in production?

options.text: One Node process uses all 8 cores for JS automatically
Run multiple Node processes (e.g., container replicas behind a LB, or `node:cluster` / PM2) — one per vCPU

questions.prompt: Select all practices that keep Node.js `worker_threads` pools efficient. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Reuse a fixed-size pool of workers rather than spawning a new `Worker` per request
Transfer ownership of `ArrayBuffer`s (`postMessage(buf, [buf])`) instead of copying large buffers
Size the worker pool based on `os.availableParallelism()` / CPU quota
Spawn 500 workers for 500 concurrent requests on a 2-vCPU container

questions.prompt: What does `os.availableParallelism()` (Node 18.14+) return compared to `os.cpus().length` in containers?

options.text: Respects container CPU cgroup quotas better as a concurrency hint

questions.prompt: Why should `NODE_ENV=production` be set in production Node deployments?

options.text: Frameworks like Express enable view/template caching and omit verbose stack traces in error responses

questions.prompt: What is a common cause of `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` when migrating a Node project to ESM (`"type": "module"`)?

options.text: Relative imports in Node ESM require explicit file extensions (`./utils.js`, not `./utils`)

questions.prompt: Match each Node.js stream or I/O failure mode to its fix.
In a Node.js microservice, what is the difference between `/healthz` (liveness) and `/readyz` (readiness)?

options.text: Liveness checks the process is alive/not deadlocked; readiness checks dependencies (DB/cache) so traffic isn't routed before ready or during shutdown

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid `Buffer.from(userString, 'base64')` or `JSON.parse` without size limits on public endpoints?

options.text: Unbounded payloads consume excessive CPU and V8/Buffer memory per request

questions.prompt: What does `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay()` measure in production Node.js?

options.text: Event-loop scheduling lag (p50/p99), revealing when synchronous code is blocking the main thread

code.source:
import { monitorEventLoopDelay } from 'node:perf_hooks';
const h = monitorEventLoopDelay(); h.enable();

questions.prompt: Select all valid ways to prevent memory leaks in long-running Node.js processes. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Store every incoming HTTP `req` object in a module-level array for debugging
Use bounded LRU caches (with max entries / TTL) instead of unbounded `new Map()`
Remove `EventEmitter` listeners on cleanup or pass `{ signal }`
Use `WeakMap` when associating metadata with ephemeral objects

questions.prompt: What does `--max-old-space-size=2048` configure in Node.js?

options.text: The V8 JavaScript heap limit (~2 GB) before garbage collection / OOM

questions.prompt: Why should Node.js containers leave headroom below the container's hard RAM limit for `Buffer`s and native addons?

options.text: `Buffer` allocations live in external/array-buffer memory outside V8's old-space JS heap

questions.prompt: Match each Node.js security header or defense to what it protects.

rows.label: Rate limiting (per IP / user / token bucket)

columns.label: Protects login/API endpoints from brute-force and DoS floods
Controls which browser origins can read API responses

questions.prompt: Why is `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` combined with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` invalid in browsers?

options.text: Browsers reject wildcard `*` with credentials; you must echo a validated origin from an explicit allowlist

questions.prompt: What does `node --experimental-strip-types app.ts` (or Node 22.18+/23+ unflagged type stripping) support?

options.text: Running `.ts` files with erasable type annotations directly without a build step
All TypeScript compiler features including `const enum` and namespaces

questions.prompt: Select all practices that improve Node.js database reliability. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Never interpolate user input into SQL strings; use `$1`/`?` bound parameters
Open a brand-new TCP database connection on every single HTTP request without closing it
Use a connection pool with bounded `max` connections and idle/acquire timeouts
Wrap multi-step writes in SQL transactions (`BEGIN` / `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK`)

questions.prompt: Why is `npm ci --omit=dev` (or multi-stage Docker build) used for Node.js production images?

options.text: To exclude devDependencies (`typescript`, `vitest`, `eslint`) from the runtime image, reducing size and attack surface

questions.prompt: What is a 'prototype pollution' sink when merging `{ ... }` recursively?
What does `stream.finished(stream)` or `pipeline()` detect that manual `'end'` listeners miss?

options.text: Premature `'close'` or `'error'` states when a client disconnects mid-response

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid `eval()`, `new Function()`, and `vm.runInNewContext()` as a security sandbox for untrusted user JS?

options.text: Node's `node:vm` module explicitly warns it is NOT a security boundary against untrusted code; use isolated processes/containers or Wasm

questions.prompt: What does `diagnostics_channel` in Node.js enable?

options.text: Zero-overhead publish/subscribe instrumentation hooks for HTTP, `fetch`, and DB libraries

questions.prompt: Match each Node.js testing strategy to what it verifies.

columns.label: Pure domain logic and edge cases in milliseconds
Real HTTP routing, status codes, middleware, and SQL queries
Request/response shapes match consumers and OpenAPI/Zod schemas

questions.prompt: Why is testing HTTP handlers with `server.listen(0)` (ephemeral port) better than hardcoding port `3000` in tests?

options.text: The OS assigns an unused port automatically, preventing `EADDRINUSE` collisions in parallel CI runs

code.source:
await new Promise((r) => server.listen(0, r));
const { port } = server.address();

questions.prompt: Select all statements that are true about `fs.watch` vs `chokidar` / polling.

options.text: Debounce file-watch callbacks because editors often emit multiple events per save
Use `--watch` for local dev, not as a critical production message queue
`fs.watch` guarantees exactly one event per byte written across all OSes
`fs.watch` behavior and duplicate events vary across Linux (inotify), macOS (FSEvents), and Windows

questions.prompt: What happens when a `Promise` rejects inside a `setTimeout` callback without a `try/catch`?

options.text: The outer `try/catch` does NOT catch it; it becomes an `unhandledRejection`

questions.prompt: Why should `crypto.randomBytes` / `randomUUID` be used instead of `Math.random()` for session IDs or password-reset tokens?

options.text: `Math.random()` is a non-cryptographic PRNG whose state can be predicted by attackers

questions.prompt: What does `zlib.createGzip()` / `zlib.createBrotliCompress()` in a stream pipeline achieve for large HTTP responses?

options.text: Compresses response chunks on the fly with low memory overhead

questions.prompt: When returning an error JSON response in production, why should you log the full `err.stack` internally while returning a generic message + `requestId` to the client?

options.text: Stack traces leak internal file paths, SQL tables, and library versions to attackers

questions.prompt: Select all valid CI checks for a production Node.js repository. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Running `npm update --force` on every production deploy

questions.prompt: What does `res.on('close', () => controller.abort())` in a streaming/SSE or slow endpoint achieve?

options.text: Cancels upstream `fetch` or DB queries immediately when the client disconnects

code.source:
const ac = new AbortController();
req.on('close', () => ac.abort());

questions.prompt: Why is `127.0.0.1` vs `0.0.0.0` important when binding `server.listen(port, host)` inside a Docker container?

options.text: Binding to `127.0.0.1` only accepts loopback connections inside the container, whereas `0.0.0.0` accepts external container/LB traffic

questions.prompt: What does `NODE_OPTIONS='--enable-source-maps'` do in production Node.js?

options.text: Translates compiled/bundled JS stack traces (from TypeScript/esbuild) back to original source file line numbers

questions.prompt: Match each Node.js architecture decision to its rationale.

columns.label: Keeps main event loop responsive for concurrent I/O
Correlates logs across async calls without threading params everywhere
Prevents OOMs and cleans up handles on client abort
